scenario: A wildlife reserve selects volunteers if they have either elite species-identification skill or elite endurance. A 5% wildcard also selects people with neither trait. Coordinators think identification skill and endurance are negatively related among volunteers.

data.description: Volunteer selection is based on either of two strengths plus a wildcard.

question: Among selected volunteers, compute (a) P(identification | endurance, selected), and (b) P(identification | not endurance, selected). Is the negative association real or induced by selection?

ground_truth.explanation: The traits are independent in the population. The volunteer rule induces the negative association.

naive_answer: Endurance and species identification appear negatively related among volunteers, so the skills likely trade off.
naive_trap: Selection on either trait creates a collider.
